name: OPA2107 (Burr-Brown/TI precision Difet JFET-input dual)
tagline: Burr-Brown Difet JFET dual (4.5 MHz, 18 V/us) that op-amp rollers call warm and full; HiFiMAN paired it with the OPA627 in its HM-801 and HM-901.
technology: Dual FET-input op-amp on Burr-Brown's proprietary dielectrically isolated (Difet) process. The datasheet says Difet keeps input bias current very low (10 pA max) without giving up offset, drift or noise. The Burr-Brown macromodel (Rev A, 10/17/90) uses a P-channel JFET input pair (.MODEL JX PJF). The datasheet and TI parametrics give 4.5 MHz GBW, 18 V/us slew and unity-gain stability. It is the faster sibling of the OPA2111 Difet dual: the 1996 EWB library gives the OPA2111 2 MHz and 2 V/us.

lineage.notes: Product data sheet PDS-863 series, (c)1989. The TI reissue header gives an original date of January 1989. Editions seen: PDS-863B (printed October 1993) and PDS-863E (printed April 1998). The BB macromodel is dated 10/17/90 Rev A. The OPA2107E model was revised 3/21/92. The 1996 EWB libraries list the AM, AP, AU, BM and SM grades.

TI reissued the datasheet as SBOS161 (rev A dated July 2003) and published a PSpice model, SBOM045. The OPA2107AP is now obsolete (DigiKey). A die broker, diedevices.com, lists OPA2107 bare die. HiFiMAN designed it into the HM-801 (2009), HM-602 (2010), HM-601LE (on sale in 2014) and HM-901 (2013). No second source is known.

reputation.summary: A cult favourite from the Head-Fi op-amp-rolling era. Forum threads (Head-Fi 'OPA2107 WOW', diyAudio), Japanese blogs and Zigsow reviews reportedly call it warm, full and tube-like, placing it between the OPA2604 and OPA627. Those pages were not re-checked. Soomal (2016) puts it in a warm, full, spacious 'DiFET' sound group, a group that also covers the OPA2134 and OPA2604, and says the OPA627/637 beat it on treble resolution. Soomal's 2013 HM-901 review admits its reviewers had not heard the OPA2107 in any other device. HiFiMAN used it in the HM-801 (with OPA627), HM-602, HM-601LE and HM-901 (OPA627 + OPA2107 in the LPF). c't Lab (2007) specifies it, or an AD712, as the input amplifier of its AD16-8 ADC card, and calls it 'weit besser' (far better) than a TL072 for the 16-bit DA12-8. No independent measurements were found.
typical_uses: DAC low-pass filter (HiFiMAN HM-901, with OPA627)
DAP analogue stage (HiFiMAN HM-801, with OPA627)
Op-amp rolling in DACs and preamps (DIP-8 OPA2107AP)
Precision high-impedance instrumentation (c't Lab AD16-8 ADC input amp)
caveats: Obsolete at TI (OPA2107AP per DigiKey), so supply is now NOS or pulled stock.
Needs a fairly high supply: Tangent measured a 10.6 V minimum (OPA627: 6.8/9.8 V). The rated range is +/-4.5 V to +/-18 V.
Modest output current (about 40 mA per the models); buffer it for low-impedance headphones.
Most sonic praise is forum or blog impression, and Soomal's 'DiFET sound' group also includes non-Difet parts (OPA2134).
Counterfeit or remark risk on NOS parts is a general concern for obsolete audio op-amps; no OPA2107-specific report was verified.

counterfeit_notes: No OPA2107-specific counterfeit report was found. The part is obsolete (OPA2107AP per DigiKey), so what is sold now is NOS, pulled or broker stock, including bare die from die brokers. General checks: see whether the logo era (BB vs TI) matches the date code, and look at marking quality and package moulding. On the bench, a genuine part should show pA-level input bias current (10 pA max), about 18 V/us slew and about 4.5 MHz GBW. A remarked bipolar part will show nA-level bias current. A remarked generic JFET dual will usually be noisier than 8 nV/rtHz at 10 kHz.

open_questions: Which mirror holds which edition (PDS-863B vs PDS-863E vs SBOS161A) was not established. Editions PDS-863 original, A, C and D and the unlettered SBOS161 were not seen.
What changed between editions is unknown.
The TI obsolescence date, the PCN/EOL notice number and the last-time-buy date were not found. The OPA2107AU and AU-2K5 statuses are not confirmed individually.
No die, fab or process change is documented. A TI-era fab transfer was neither confirmed nor ruled out.
The quiescent-current discrepancy is unresolved: the datasheet text says under 2.5 mA per amplifier, while a parametric listing gives 4.5 mA 'per channel'.
The 1 kHz noise, i_n, THD+N and guaranteed Aol/CMRR datasheet values were not captured. Aol and CMRR in this record are model values.
When the TO-99 grades (AM, BM, SM) were dropped is unknown; the TO-99 package is inferred.
The contents of the 1990 bitsavers data-book supplement were not checked.
The forum and blog reputation pages were not re-checked.
Whether the original HM-601 (not LE) used the OPA2107 is unverified.

refuted_claims: The draft said the Burr-Brown PDS number and first-release date were unknown and dated the part only 'by 1990'. The datasheet is PDS-863, (c)1989, and the TI header gives an original date of January 1989.
The looser 'early-to-mid 1990s design' framing is contradicted by the January 1989 original date.
The draft said the TI datasheet literature number was unknown. It is SBOS161, rev A, July 2003.
corrections: Datasheets: SBOS161A (TI, July 2003) was added as vendor_current at ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2107.pdf, with high confidence. The ti.com/product/OPA2107 folder was confirmed and raised to high. The ti.com/lit/gpn link was added.
Revision history: PDS-863B (October 1993), PDS-863E (April 1998) and SBOS161A (July 2003) were added, plus an inferred January 1989 original.

Mirrors added at low confidence: pdf.dzsc.com, www2.ung.si (university), farnell.com/datasheets/9308.pdf, datasheetspdf 475543, manualmachine, chipfind, alldatasheet TI2 2195756, eicom.ru, radiolocman, and the bitsavers 1990 BB data-book supplement. Which edition each holds is not identified.
Part numbers: OPA2107AP set to Obsolete (DigiKey). OPA2107AU-2K5 (tape and reel) was added.

Key specs: datasheet headline limits were added (8 nV/rtHz at 10 kHz, Vos 1 mV max, drift 10 uV/C max, IB 10 pA max, settling 2 us to 0.01%). GBW 4.5 MHz and slew 18 V/us now cite TI/distributor parametrics. The supply range is +/-4.5 V to +/-18 V. Iq is under 2.5 mA per amplifier, with the conflicting 4.5 mA parametric figure noted. The EWB 'max supply field' entry was replaced by the datasheet range.
ti_literature_numbers now includes SBOS161. More archive seeds were added (TI gpn, Farnell, ung.si, dzsc, bitsavers).

Discovery hazard hint: 'obsolete' is confirmed. 'High risk of remarked fakes' remains a general concern with no OPA2107-specific evidence. No silicon change or PCN was found, so silicon_changes stays empty.
claims_confirmed: The TI datasheet is SBOS161A, 'January 1989 - revised July 2003', hosted at https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2107.pdf

The Burr-Brown data sheet PDS-863B was printed October 1993 and PDS-863E April 1998, both (c)1989. Search summary over the Burr-Brown mirrors, e.g. https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/177039/BURR-BROWN/OPA2107.html
The TI product folder exists: https://www.ti.com/product/OPA2107

Datasheet features: 8 nV/rtHz at 10 kHz, Vos 1 mV max, drift 10 uV/C max, IB 10 pA max, 2 us settling to 0.01%, unity-gain stable, Difet dielectrically isolated process: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2107.pdf
GBW 4.5 MHz, slew 18 V/us, supply +/-4.5 V to +/-18 V (9-36 V): https://www.industrycomponent.com/en/index.php?main_page=product_info&products_id=2165455
Quiescent current is under 2.5 mA per amplifier (datasheet text), in DIP-8 and SO-8 packages: https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/9308.pdf

revision_chain_notes:
Searches used: 6 of 6.

BURR-BROWN PDS-863 (oldest to newest):
(1) Original edition, January 1989. The date is inferred from the SBOS161A header and the (c)1989 notice. The letter (unlettered or A) has not been seen, and no copy was found. The 1989 BB IC Data Book and the 1990 Supplement 33b on bitsavers/archive.org are the best candidates for its content.
(2) PDS-863B, printed October 1993. Copies: alldatasheet 177039 (already listed, low) and its HTML view at html.alldatasheet.com (new). A search summary also tied PDS-863B / October 1993 to the ung.si copy (www2.ung.si/~sstanic/belle/monitor/schemes/bb2107.pdf). That copy is listed as 'unknown', so upgrade it to probably B at low-medium confidence.
(3) PDS-863C and (4) PDS-863D: still MISSING. Their dates and copies were not found.
(5) PDS-863E, printed April 1998. Copy: pdf.dzsc.com (already listed). Its front page shows 'LOW VOS: 1mV max'.
The rtellason.com copy has 'LOW VOS: 500µV max', so it is an edition earlier than E; its letter is not shown.

TEXAS INSTRUMENTS SBOS161:
(a) Unlettered SBOS161, about 2000-2001 after the TI takeover: still MISSING. No copy or date was found, and a search that excluded 'SBOS161A' returned nothing for it.
(b) SBOS161A, 'January 1989 - Revised July 2003': ti.com symlink and gpn (already listed). New mirror: datasheet4u ID 475543, which a search summary says holds SBOS161A. The already-listed datasheetspdf.com/pdf/475543 copy and the new datasheet-pdf.com 475543 copy are probably the same TI file, not a Burr-Brown PDS edition.
The Farnell 9308 copy's title uses the mixed-case TI layout ('FEATURES Very Low Noise ... Low VOS: 1mV max'), the same as ti.com/lit/gpn. It therefore probably holds an SBOS161-family edition, not PDS-863 (inference, low confidence).
SBOS161A appears to be the last revision; no B was seen.

OTHER VENDORS: No second source was found.

NEW COPIES, EDITION NOT SHOWN: alldatasheet 177040 (AP) and 177041 (AU), both 685 KB and 11 pages; datasheetcatalog OPA2107, OPA2107AP and OPA2107AU; digchip; datasheetarchive; RadioLocman di=305535; Octopart and Mouser product pages.

ARCHIVE SEED: http://focus.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/opa2107.pdf. This URL was not seen in any search result. It was built from TI's standard legacy symlink pattern and the current ti.com symlink, for a Wayback lookup only.

STILL MISSING: the original or PDS-863A text; PDS-863C and PDS-863D; the unlettered SBOS161 and its date; the change content of every revision; the burr-brown.com-era URL (not found).
